input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
task: Flagship 8 quick-pick-survey, item (b): do answer times see half-time salience pickers?

errors.what: First sweep launch used the script's default --pace-min 0.6 instead of the shipped FAST_PACE 0.5; caught after 5 cells, killed and relaunched.
The full 240-cell grid at 40 surveys would have taken about 2.5 h on 4 CPUs; trimmed to 132 cells (dissent at one ratio, since ratio does not touch a camp; random and q = 1 at gamma 0.6).
venture-preflight failed on inherited_keys.py scanning the gitignored .next build left by npm run verify; removed .next and reran.
Appending to quick-pick-survey's flagships next: took it to 2229 characters, over validate.py's 2000 cap; rewrote it replacing the landed item.

doc_friction.issue: --pace-min defaults to 0.6 while the shipped FAST_PACE is 0.5 and the doc table reports 'pace-drop 0.5'; easy to run the sweep at the wrong threshold.

inherited_keys.py scans the gitignored .next directory, so running `npm run verify` (which builds) before the preflight fails it on Next's own bundled code; the preflight should skip .next or say to delete it.

goal: Deepen flagship 8 with a measured, shipped answer to item (b).
notes: answer-time-sweep.ts takes --q (q = 1 reproduces the 2026-11-12 rows exactly; replay of Glicko states checked against simulate). Per-person pace recovers 0-35% of the ceiling against half-time salience pickers; a per-answer cut recovers 55-75% at 0.4x pace, 20-42% at 0.6x; costs 0.000-0.006 with nobody careless, 0.002-0.019 against a camp. Shipped ?drop=fast-answers (ratingsWithoutFastAnswers replays trials in answeredAt order) and a builder button; default unchanged. Verification: npm run verify (typecheck, lint, 528 unit tests, build) green; integration suite 123 tests green on scripts/test-db.sh Postgres; the replay test goes red when answers are replayed in reverse order; the cut-edge unit test goes red on <= instead of <. venture-preflight clean (after removing .next and trimming flagships next: under its 2000-character cap).

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: a statistician-engineer extending a simulation sweep, running 132 cells, writing the per-answer replay with route, UI and tests, and the write-up and post

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
